analysis.title: US midterms put Congress in play (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: UBS CIO says a Democratic 'blue sweep' (control of both House and Senate) is the highest-probability midterm outcome, with consensus building around it. The Senate remains closely fought and the size of any majority is uncertain.

Polls show Trump's net approval at -20pps (RCP average), -32pps on the economy and -43pps on inflation. Democrats lead the generic congressional ballot by 8.9pps. Early voting turnout has favored Democrats more than in 2024 in several key states, but around half of the national vote has come on Election Day in recent elections.
The result may not be clear in the first hours after polls close. Mail-in ballots, close races and Alaska's ranked-choice system could delay calls, and election litigation is already under way.

Even with a Democratic win of both chambers, narrow majorities, Senate rules, party divisions and Trump's veto would constrain major legislative change. UBS advises against treating the midterms as a binary market event.
UBS expects the outcome to be unlikely to displace the main market drivers: AI investment, economic growth, corporate earnings, inflation and interest rates.

A change in congressional control would bring more oversight and harder fiscal negotiations, but not automatically big changes to tax or spending. The executive keeps broad authority over tariffs and foreign policy, which leaves room for volatility.

The 2027 debt ceiling talks are the clearest bond risk. UBS thinks they could soften scheduled social program cuts and raise defense spending, which could reverse an expected narrowing in deficits and increase Treasury supply. Brinkmanship could raise bond volatility.

UBS still expects inflation to moderate, the Fed to finish raising rates, and Treasury yields to settle lower. It sees attractive income in high-quality bonds, favors short- to medium-term maturities and stays cautious on the longest maturities because of deficits and heavy issuance.

AI capex forecasts were raised to USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027 (USD 1.5tr in 2028). Investors are weighting overinvestment, financing and monetization risks more heavily, and UBS expects higher volatility to persist. It favors financially strong platforms, infrastructure providers and diversified exposure across the AI value chain.

UBS recommends avoiding large positions based on a binary political result, reducing single-name concentration, rebalancing oversized technology exposure and tilting within tech toward quality AI value chain companies. It keeps a constructive view on equities, backed by earnings and AI investment.

On Monday the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.4% into technical correction territory, 10.4% below its 6 October peak. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.4%. The equal-weighted S&P 500 rose 0.7% with more than two-thirds of constituents advancing, helped by lower oil prices and easing geopolitical concerns.
Apple fell about 3% after hours. It slightly beat third-quarter sales expectations but guided gross margin down to 45-46% this quarter.

UBS reads the tech sell-off as a shift in the AI debate from spending commitments toward monetization, balance sheet strength and returns. It says recent earnings reinforced confidence in AI demand, citing accelerating cloud revenue and stronger hyperscaler spending commitments.

vol_and_positioning: The Nasdaq 100 is in technical correction territory, 10.4% below its 6 October peak, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.4% on Monday.
UBS says higher volatility could become the new normal in AI, and suggests using volatility to rebalance or build exposure gradually.
The equal-weighted S&P 500 gained 0.7% with more than two-thirds of constituents advancing, which shows a rotation away from mega-cap tech.
UBS expects the 2027 debt ceiling negotiations and political brinkmanship could raise bond market volatility.
geopolitical: US midterm elections on 3-4 November 2026, with all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats contested.
Easing geopolitical concerns and lower oil prices supported the broader equity market on Monday.

tension_points.what_invalidates: A material surprise in the size or composition of the majority, which could shift perceptions of the 2028 race.
